title: "Introduction to R"

Welcome to Introduction to R!

## Course Overview

- This ad-hoc website intends to help students self-study R programming.
- Students will learn how to manipulate data, perform statistical and econometric analysis, and visualize data using R. 
 

## Artificial Intelligence (AI)
- I highly encourage students to use AIs to learn R (and other) programming. 
- Use AIs wisely. 
- Nowadays, you can vibe-code R scripts with AI assistants. 
  - You describe what you want to do in natural language. Then the AI agent generates and execute the code on your behalf. 
  - So you do not necessarily have to memorize every single command. You can always ask or delegate coding tasks to AIs. 
- But you still need to know basics and big pictures because
  - you need to ask and frame your questions properly.  
  - AIs make mistakes, and you have to catch their mistakes.
- Always check and verify what AIs do or suggest. Ultimately, you are the one who bears responsibility for the outcomes and final products from data analysis. 

## Useful Resources

### Official Websites
- [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) 
- [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/downloads)
- [Official RStudio user guide](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/)

### Textbooks: Data Analysis 
- [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/)

### Textbooks: Econometrics
- [Using R, Python and Julia for Introductory Econometrics](https://www.urfie.net/) by Florian Heiss: This free textbook is an empirical companion to *Introductory Econometrics* by Jeffrey M. Wooldridge.
  - [Using R for Introductory Econometrics](https://www.urfie.net/downloads/PDF/URfIE_web.pdf)
- [Introduction to Econometrics with R](https://www.econometrics-with-r.org/): This free textbook is an empirical companion to *Introduction to Econometrics* by Stock and Watson, another standard econometrics textbook.      

### Publicly Available Datasets
- [IPUMS](https://www.ipums.org/)
